task.title: Background clipping, shorthand and blending
task.shortdesc: These CSS properties specify the area where a background is painted, combine background settings in one declaration, and control how image layers combine.

info.p: “CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.8, Painting Area: the background-clip property”.
Use background-clip to specify how far a background color or image extends across an element’s box.

border-box allows the background to extend beneath the border, padding-box clips it at the outside edge of the padding, and content-box clips it to the content area. border-area clips it to the area covered by the border. text clips it to the shape of the text glyphs. border-area and text can be combined. The CSS initial value is border-box. Separate values for multiple image layers with commas.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.12, Backgrounds Shorthand: the background property”.

Use background to specify several background properties in one declaration. For each layer, you can provide an image, position and size, repeat style, attachment and clipping or positioning boxes. Set the background color in the final layer.

The slash separates background-position from background-size. A box value can set both the positioning and painting areas. Two box values set the positioning area first and the painting area second. The CSS shorthand resets its longhand properties to their initial values when you leave them out. It also resets background-blend-mode to normal.
Use background-blend-mode to specify how each background image layer combines with the layer below it and the element’s background color.

The available modes are normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, color-dodge, color-burn, hard-light, soft-light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color and luminosity. The first value applies to the top image layer. If the list has fewer values than the image list, the values repeat. The CSS initial value is normal.
